Cheap suspicion signal used (not one of ①-④ as literally defined, but the same spirit as ③ "matrix divergence" — a same-commit, zero-code-reading comparison): the **paired PR-merge-queue run of this exact same commit** (https://github.com/growilabs/growi/actions/runs/32458546547, same commit `a7bbb57`, running 3 seconds later) ran the identical job `ci-app-test-integration (24.x, 8.0, 9, 9.3.3)` and it **passed**. Same commit, same matrix cell, same job definition, two near-simultaneous runs, opposite outcomes — this is same-commit divergent-outcome evidence, just across the push/PR-merge run pair rather than within a single run's differing matrix cells.

PR #11739 ("fix: stabilize flaky emacs-keymap bold/link tests") is the only PR associated with this commit — a Playwright emacs-keymap test fix, unrelated to `test/setup/migrate-mongo.ts` or any of the 3 affected integration specs (diff/PR mismatch, ①, also holds).

precondition directly instead of looping to it): the cost here is a
one-time subprocess spawn + migration run, not a loop over a test
parameter, so there is no obvious O(1) substitute for "run the
migrations". A bare timeout bump would be treating the symptom (this
hook loses the race under CI load) without addressing why it's on the
edge of its budget in the first place.

autonomous fix: `dev:migrate:up` runs independently per worker today

spec), so it stays MEDIUM confidence per this skill's Step 4 gate.

### Investigation — root cause identified, confidence gate: MEDIUM (stop for human decision)

**Category (Step 3)**: Environment timing / Driver 2 (concurrent setup work), but with a concrete, previously-undiscovered *structural* defect underneath — not just "runner contention."

**Root cause**: `test/setup/migrate-mongo.ts`'s own comment (added by #11828's fix) already documents that this hook "genuinely runs once per file, not once per worker despite the `migrationsRun` guard" — Vitest's `forks` pool resets the module registry per test file under `isolate: true`, so the `let migrationsRun = false` closure is **not** shared across files the way the guard's own logic assumes. Every one of the ~135 `app-integration` spec files pays a full `execSync('pnpm run dev:migrate:up')` subprocess spawn (its own Node process running every migration through the dev TS runner + a MongoDB round-trip per migration) — not once per worker as the guard comment intends, but once per **file**.

#11828's `--poolOptions.forks.maxForks=4` fix (still in place — verified in `apps/app/package.json`) caps *concurrent* forks to 4, which cut the failure rate substantially (documented: ~80%→~1% in that PR's own local repro), but does not remove the per-file redundant spawn itself. Under any renewed load spike (the two occurrences that reopened this issue and #11821 both came from an unusually long-running job — 651-698s vs. a typical ~450s), 4 concurrent workers each independently re-spawning this subprocess as they cycle through files is still enough to blow the 20s hook budget on whichever file draws the short straw.

**Why this is MEDIUM, not HIGH**: the structurally correct fix — moving the migration to a Vitest `globalSetup` hook (runs once in the main process, before any worker starts, with no per-file/per-worker ambiguity at all) instead of a per-file `setupFiles` `beforeAll` — was already proposed for this exact issue on 2026-08-21 (see the first comment on this issue) and explicitly deferred as "a more structural option worth a human's judgment call... broader than this skill should make autonomously (it touches shared test infra for every integration worker, not a single spec)." That reasoning still holds: this change affects the setup behavior of every `app-integration`/`app-integration-exclusive` spec file, not a single test.

**Recommendation**: move `runMigrations()` from `test/setup/migrate-mongo.ts`'s per-file `beforeAll` into a `globalSetup` entry in the relevant Vitest project config, guarded so it truly runs once for the whole test session. This removes the redundant per-file subprocess spawn entirely (not just bounding its concurrency), which directly addresses the recurrence rather than re-tuning `maxForks` or the hook timeout again. A human should review this given the blast radius (every integration spec's setup path) before it's implemented autonomously.

No code change made this run — pausing this issue per this routine's autonomous-mode policy for MEDIUM-confidence gates; continuing with the rest of the queue.

### Reproduction

This issue was created from a same-commit rerun flip (attempt 1 failed with this exact `MongoNotConnectedError`, attempt 2 passed with no code change) — the flakiness itself is already empirically confirmed; no further rerun was needed to establish that. A second independent occurrence was recorded on 2026-08-27T19:08:13Z (see the "Additional observation" comment on this issue), on a different MongoDB-version matrix cell — same identity, same signature.

### Root Cause (same underlying bug as #11707)

The unhandled rejection surfaces at the very end of the whole `ci-app-test-integration` run (after the last suite, `test/setup/crowi.integ.ts`, has already reported success) — vitest's own note ("this error originated in `external-user-group-sync.integ.ts`... doesn't mean the error was thrown inside the file itself") is accurate here: this is a leftover async operation from that test, not a bug in the test's own assertions.

This is the same race already root-caused on #11707 for a different symptom (an off-by-one page count assertion): `ExternalUserGroupSyncService.getMemberUser()` → `externalAccountService.getOrCreateUser()` → `User.createUser()` fires the `'activated'` event **without awaiting it**:

```js
// apps/app/src/server/models/user/index.js:729-739
newUser.save((err, userData) => {
  ...
  if (userData.status === UserStatus.STATUS_ACTIVE) {
    userEvent.emit('activated', userData); // fire-and-forget
  }
  return callback(err, userData); // resolves before onActivated settles
});
```

`onActivated()` (`apps/app/src/server/events/user.ts:23-56`) is `async` and calls `pageService.create(...)`, which (per `apps/app/src/server/service/page/index.ts`) issues `Page.updateMany(...)` calls as part of updating ancestor/descendant bookkeeping for the newly created user-home page. Because the `'activated'` emit is never awaited, this `updateMany` keeps running in the background after `syncExternalUserGroups()` resolves.

In #11707's occurrence, the race was narrow enough that the operation merely lost to the *test's own* final assertion (page count off by one). In this occurrence, the operation was delayed long enough to survive past the **entire test run** — by the time it actually executes, global teardown has already closed the MongoDB client, producing `MongoNotConnectedError: Client must be connected before running operations` as an unhandled rejection instead of a failed assertion. Same root cause, different timing outcome.

The fix is not local to this test or even to `external-user-group-sync.ts` — it requires awaiting the `onActivated` listener at the three `userEvent.emit('activated', ...)` call sites in `apps/app/src/server/models/user/index.js` (shared by every user-activation path: local signup, LDAP, OIDC, admin-created users, etc.). That is real, valuable product-code work, but it is a broader change than this flaky-test issue's scope, and #11707 already recommended scoping it as its own separate piece of work rather than folding it into a flaky-test fix.

### Recommendation

Do not fix in this issue. Recommend:
1. A dedicated follow-up task (referencing both #11707 and this issue) to make the three `userEvent.emit('activated', ...)` call sites in `apps/app/src/server/models/user/index.js` await `onActivated` before resolving `createUser()` — with its own test coverage for the ordering guarantee.

**What was measured.** No confirmation measurement is owed for this identity: it is a
Playwright in-run retry, which is already the empirical proof of non-determinism

https://github.com/growilabs/growi/actions/runs/34826447171 , job
`test-prod-node24 / run-playwright (chromium, 1/2, 8.0)`). The `flaky-repro` workflow's
project allowlist is vitest-only, so no repro request applies here.

**Root cause (Step 3 category: missing await / race in the test).** In
`apps/app/playwright/20-basic-features/inline-comment.spec.ts`, the body-popover
describe block creates the saved inline comment in its first test and there waits for the
highlight to actually exist before going on:

```ts
await expect
  .poll(async () =>
    page.evaluate(() => CSS.highlights.get('growi-inline-comment')?.size ?? 0),
  )
  .toBeGreaterThan(0);
```

The four later tests in the same block (lines ~2011, ~2040, ~2063, ~2077) each navigate to
the page again and then wait only for `inline-comment-ready` to be *attached* before
calling `clickText(page, targetSentence)` / `hoverText(...)`. That marker says the
SelectionCapture component reached its idle stage; it does not say the saved anchor has
been resolved and the hit-testable `CSS.highlights` Range registered. On a fresh load the
resolution is asynchronous, so a click can land before the Range exists, the hit test
matches nothing, no popover opens, and the very next line
(`await expect(popover).toBeVisible()`, line 2085) times out after 7000ms with
`element(s) not found` — exactly the recorded failure. The three sibling tests doing the
same sequence normally win the race, which is why this shows up as flakiness rather than
a hard failure.

**Fix approach reached (HIGH).** Test-side and surgical, one file: wait for
`CSS.highlights.get('growi-inline-comment')?.size > 0` after `inline-comment-ready` in the
four tests that interact with the highlight — the same poll the first test already uses —
ideally factored into a small helper next to `clickText` / `hoverText` so the next test
added to this block inherits it. No product-code change is implied.

**Why this is paused rather than fixed.** This run is the validation cycle for task 6.3 of
the `flaky-ci-closed-loop` spec, and the operator explicitly deferred Step 5 onward for
this run: no fix branch was pushed and no PR was opened. The investigation is therefore
complete up to and including the fix-approach decision, and stops there. Nothing is being
watched; the next routine run picks this issue up once a human has answered.
